explanation: The L100I substitution increases hydrophobicity while maintaining nearly identical side-chain volume, which disrupts the precise van der Waals contact geometry between the pocket rim and etravirine at ~7.6 Å distance. Although isoleucine's branched β-carbon configuration creates a more constrained conformational space than leucine's flexible γ-carbon, this geometric restriction at the pocket perimeter forces subtle repositioning of the inhibitor or local protein backbone to accommodate the altered hydrophobic landscape, destabilizing the bound state by ~0.28 kcal/mol. This mechanism exemplifies how rim mutations attenuate NNRTI binding through cumulative disruption of the hydrophobic complementarity rather than through direct steric clash or loss of critical interactions.
